name: Maelis Vorne
appearance: Small and somewhere in her fifties, with a deeply lined, weathered face, steady grey eyes and a few old nicks of scar at the corner of her mouth and chin. Her grey hair is pulled back and worn in a long braid over one shoulder; she dresses for the cold in a worn dark coat and a frayed wool scarf, and her forearms are seamed with old scars, her fingers stained with ink. A clay pipe of bitterleaf stays clamped in her teeth, unlit, and shifts from one side of her mouth to the other when she is deciding something. She can sit for a long time with two fingers on a joint and her eyes shut, and when she opens them and looks at a man properly, it is worse than the Reading.
portrait_alt: Portrait of Maelis Vorne: a lined, weathered woman in her fifties with steady grey eyes, grey hair in a long braid over one shoulder, an unlit clay pipe in her teeth, a worn dark coat and frayed scarf, in a stone room with a snowy mountain window on one side and a fire on the other.
last_seen_doing: Came down to the kennels with bad grace and re-splinted the hound in pine and linen; watched the Captain take his hand off the cold grate, and left without a word.
now: Gone back up from the kennels. She has seen the Captain's hand go to the drain grate and come away.
story_so_far: She took him down at her count and brought him up at it, knew the way east before he asked, laid her hand on a handleless door and said to leave it, and breathed the cold at the far wall as if it were air. She stopped his hand once; the second time she waited to see if he would go, and said up when the frost had stopped at his knuckles. It is the second time she has seen a hand go into one of those.

quote.text: The slow way, Captain. Every time. Or I'll have Wren count your steps and read me the number at every bell.

known_facts.fact: She was standing in the gate at the top of the Thousand Steps, small and grey-braided with her arms folded, when the litter carrying Darrow reached the top.
She read Darrow's knee with two fingers and her eyes shut and judged it not broken but undone: the cord in the middle, snapped, with no blow behind it.
When Darrow said the knee had held fine for thirty-two years, she answered that it had help for twelve of them, watched his face while she said it, and did not explain what she meant.
known_facts.evidence: but she watched his face while she said it

known_facts.fact: She refused to touch the knee for six weeks, because a Binding takes the measure of whatever it is tied to and a weak leg would give him a weak knee.

She keeps a wooden box holding a curved needle and a spool of emberthread that glows like a blown coal, an old art whose practitioners the Crown burned three hundred years ago, and she asked Darrow not to tell anyone she practices it.
She performed the Binding with her bitterleaf pipe unlit in her teeth, saying very quietly, as if to someone who wasn't there, "Time makes it possible. Proof makes it permitted."
She told Darrow he could not kneel after the Binding, not for a long time and perhaps not ever.
By Wren Ashdown's ledger at the head of the chapter, the captain of the Ninth has asked fourteen times whether he may go down the Steps, and Mender Vorne has said no fourteen times.
Asked how many Bindings she has done, she said only that it was enough to know what the soft season looks like, and agreed that was not a number.
known_facts.evidence: Enough to know what the soft season looks like

known_facts.fact: When Darrow saw the script of light above his palms, she did not look surprised; she said "So it's begun" and told him to close the door.
known_facts.evidence: She didn't look surprised. That frightened him more than the light had.

known_facts.fact: She was shut in a cell down the hall with the Captain while Hollis hid the writ; nothing came through the door, and at the end of the Interlude a latch lifted and it opened.
In her cell she told Darrow there are two fires a man can carry, one poured in and one built, that the script reads only what is one's own, and that no one full of Grace has ever seen it.

She named the order that lived by the built fire, burned by the Crown three hundred years ago, and forbade Darrow to speak of it in the hall, to Wren, the Prior, or Hollis most of all, because Hollis is second on a list and she wants his honest answer to be nothing.
Asked how she knows all this, she said only that she is a Mender and Menders remember things.
known_facts.evidence: I'm a Mender. We remember things.

known_facts.fact: When Darrow argued that Hollis was owed the knowing of the built fire, she said Hollis is owed a leg and will get a wooden one, that a Confessor watches a man's mouth while he answers, that Hollis must be able to answer with nothing and mean it, and that when he asks, Darrow will lie to him.
known_facts.evidence: Let Hollis answer with nothing and mean it

known_facts.fact: Behind the cell door she told Darrow that the Confessors don't need him to tell them anything, they need to see the knee: any Confessor who lays a hand on it will know what's in it, and the Crown has burned every hand it ever caught putting it there.
known_facts.evidence: the Crown has burned every hand it ever caught putting it there

known_facts.fact: Of the Grace: she has had her fingers on knees that carried it for twenty years; it holds things up, it doesn't mend them, and a man can run on a torn thing a long while with it under him and never know. Of Faithless: a word for a knight the Grace has left, which says it left because of him.
known_facts.evidence: It holds things up, Captain. It doesn't mend them.

known_facts.fact: Told the Grace was taken rather than lost, she agreed that then somebody took it, a finding and not a side, and said she was up here that day with her hands in another man's leg: what it did at the ford, and whose doing, she does not know.
known_facts.evidence: What it did at the ford, and whose doing, I don't know

known_facts.fact: At the Prior's council she gave the law: while Old Mercy rings at dawn and dusk, no blade climbs the Steps or passes the gate, and no name under it is taken down against its will; miss one ringing and the law lapses till the next.
known_facts.evidence: no name under it is taken down against its will

known_facts.fact: When Darrow asked the council to send him down on the cage before the grey cloaks came, she answered for the fifteenth time, to the fire and without looking round, that the answer is the same as the other fourteen and will be the same at fifty: the thread is soft, eleven hundred steps down are eleven hundred chances to tear it, and the cage is for salt.
known_facts.evidence: Fifteen, Captain, and the answer's the same as the other fourteen

known_facts.fact: When Darrow asked the council to send him down on the cage, she said that if he reached the bottom whole they would put him on his knees on a stone, the thread would go, and she does not do this twice.
known_facts.evidence: they put you on your knees on a stone

known_facts.fact: She stood a pace behind Mother Ione's shoulder at the gate while the Confessor read; when his eyes went past the Prior to her and stayed a beat longer than courtesy, she looked back at him with the pipe clamped and nothing in her face at all.
known_facts.evidence: nothing in her face at all

known_facts.fact: After the wicket she saw to the bloodied lay brother first, two fingers under his jaw, and asked after his teeth; then she came to Darrow, looked at the knee first and then at his face, and took the pipe out to say that hidden he was a lie they'd have found by the thaw, and named he is a law they'll have to break where the valley can watch; the knee lies to her every morning, he hadn't, and he was to keep it that way. She sent him to the hall slowly and said she would read the knee tonight.
known_facts.evidence: That knee lies to me every morning

known_facts.fact: Reading the knee by lamplight on the night of the gate, she found it had held at the wicket, and said what one moment more of a man's weight on that door would have cost: nothing left to tie it to.
known_facts.evidence: I'd have had nothing left to tie it to

known_facts.fact: Having found it held, she said it is still soft, and will be soft at the thaw.
known_facts.evidence: It'll be soft at the thaw.

known_facts.fact: On the feast morning she found a chip of black glass under Hollowed Benedek's tongue, looked down the hall at the far cots, said the far cots never had this, and took it away folded in linen inside her coat.
known_facts.evidence: She lifted the chip out onto a square of linen

known_facts.fact: Asked what the glass was, she would say only that it was not the far cots' sickness, and that the rest she would say when she knew it and not in the hall.
known_facts.evidence: Not the far cots' sickness.

known_facts.fact: She saw the Captain get up off his cot before he had decided to, watched the knee take it and hold, and ordered him to take the slow way every time or she would have Wren count his steps.
known_facts.evidence: Next time, decide first.

known_facts.fact: She sent the Captain to make Hollis eat, because Hollis would not for her.
known_facts.evidence: He won't for me.

known_facts.fact: When Marrant's word, ember witchcraft, reached the hall and heads turned toward her, the Captain told the hall that nobody passed, not the Mender either.
known_facts.evidence: Not the Mender.

known_facts.fact: She knew his step: she was already looking at the door when he came in.
known_facts.evidence: She knew his step.

known_facts.fact: She keeps the black glass from Benedek's mouth folded in linen inside her coat; three days on, the cold still comes off it.
known_facts.evidence: It had been three days inside her coat, against her ribs

known_facts.fact: When the Captain's hand went toward the glass she caught his wrist, held it a moment longer than she needed to, and her face went very still.
known_facts.evidence: her face went very still

known_facts.fact: Asked what the glass is, she made the Captain say what it looked like, and did not say no to a chip off a field-stone.
known_facts.evidence: Maelis did not say no.

known_facts.fact: She told him that if he said so in the hall, Marrant would ask how a Mender came by a piece of one; it clears her when she can prove it, not before.
known_facts.evidence: Marrant will ask how a Mender came by a piece of one

known_facts.fact: When the House turned to her in front of the gate, she did not move; one hand lay flat on her coat over the linen.
known_facts.evidence: One hand lay flat on her coat, over the place where the linen was.

known_facts.fact: When the Captain moved to speak for her in front of the gate, she stopped him with one shake of the head.
known_facts.evidence: she moved her head once: no

known_facts.fact: While the Prior spoke, her hand went flat to a place on the door's frame worn pale and smooth, the way a hand goes to a post it has leaned on in the dark; she took it away when the Captain looked.
known_facts.evidence: the way a hand goes to a post it has leaned on in the dark

known_facts.fact: She stood at the foot of the Grey Cot where the whole House could see her; nobody had told her to.
known_facts.evidence: Maelis stood at the foot of the Grey Cot, where the whole House could see her

known_facts.fact: When the Captain kept the glass out of the hall, she was looking at his face and not the knee.
known_facts.evidence: for once she was looking at his face, not the knee

known_facts.fact: She did not sit on the stool the lay brother set behind her, and did not move it.
known_facts.evidence: Maelis did not sit on it. She did not move it, either.

known_facts.fact: Asked whether she had been down the undercroft stair, she asked the Captain what the knee did this morning; it was not a no.
known_facts.evidence: "What did the knee do this morning, Captain?"

known_facts.fact: She told the Captain he has never waited for anything in his life.
known_facts.evidence: You've never waited for anything in your life.

known_facts.fact: She told him not tonight, not on that leg: to ask again tomorrow and the day after, and that she will tell him when the leg will bear him on a stair.
known_facts.evidence: Not tonight. Not on that leg. Ask me again tomorrow, Captain, and the day after.

known_facts.fact: Asked again, she asked him first what he will do at the bottom of the stair.
known_facts.evidence: Then I'll ask you something first. What will you do at the bottom?

known_facts.fact: She told him his answer, to come back up on this leg, is the right one and is not true yet, and to ask her tomorrow.
known_facts.evidence: That's the right answer," she said. "It isn't true yet. Ask me tomorrow.

known_facts.fact: At the hour she did not read the knee at his cot; she read it at the foot of the warming-room stair instead.
known_facts.evidence: for once she did not read the knee

known_facts.fact: She read the leg, after the warming-room stair, as able to take a stair.
known_facts.evidence: That's a stair

known_facts.fact: Unasked, she said she would take him down the undercroft stair at dusk: her count, Wren's shoulder.
known_facts.evidence: Tell the Prior I'll take you down

known_facts.fact: She would rather fewer people watched him do it.
known_facts.evidence: I'd rather fewer people watched you do it

known_facts.fact: She said it is as dark below at noon as at midnight, and to Darrow it did not sound like a guess.
known_facts.evidence: She had said it the way she said what a knee would do. Not as a guess.

known_facts.fact: She put the words over the inner door into plain speech.
known_facts.evidence: She said it flat, to the lintel

known_facts.fact: She told Wren she will not hear those words in the hall.
known_facts.evidence: You'll not hear it in the hall.

known_facts.fact: She walked the undercroft hall in the dark without a lamp.
known_facts.evidence: She went round a fallen block of stone without looking down at it

known_facts.fact: She held him to his word: look, then come up.
known_facts.evidence: You said you'd look, then come up. You've looked.

known_facts.fact: She knew which way to go in the undercroft before he asked: east, the pillars on the right.
known_facts.evidence: "East," Maelis said, from behind them, before he had asked.

known_facts.fact: She put her hand flat on the handleless door, low, and left it there a moment before wiping it on her coat and telling him to leave that one.
known_facts.evidence: She put her hand flat on the grey wood, low down, where a hand would go to push, and left it there.

known_facts.fact: She breathed the cold at the far wall as if the air were air, without lamp or cloak.
known_facts.evidence: breathed as if the air were air

known_facts.fact: She stopped his hand at the alcove: not with his hand, not today.
known_facts.evidence: "Not with your hand," she said. "Not today."

known_facts.fact: She said yes, it is in the wall under the lad's cot, and yes, somebody put it there.
known_facts.evidence: "Yes." She let go of his wrist.

known_facts.fact: She made him promise, in words, that if she says up it is up at once, not after the next thing.
known_facts.evidence: "If I say up," she said, "it's up. At once. Not after the next thing."

known_facts.fact: She let him take the bar and go down on the right knee, and did not take his wrist this time.
known_facts.evidence: she stood at his shoulder in the cold with her arms folded inside her sleeves, breathing, and let him go down onto the right knee, and watched which

known_facts.fact: She did not say up when he refused to leave the thing, and let him put his hand in.
known_facts.evidence: She did not answer that. She did not say up, either.

known_facts.fact: She says this is the second time she has seen a hand go into one of those, and that the first man kept his.
known_facts.evidence: "That's the second time I've seen a hand go into one of those. The first man kept his."

known_facts.fact: She says she waited before saying up because she wanted to see if he would go.
known_facts.evidence: "I wanted to see if you'd go."

known_facts.fact: She says he will have the use of the hand by the dawn bell, the ends of the fingers not for a week, and is not to put it near the stone again.
known_facts.evidence: The ends of the fingers, not for a week.

known_facts.fact: She said it will not be her who carries it to the Prior, and she will not be standing beside him when he does.
known_facts.evidence: It won't be me who carries it, and I'll not be standing beside you when you do.

known_facts.fact: She took the second wrapped thing from the almoner's satchel into her coat without a word about it.
known_facts.evidence: she closed her fingers on it and looked at nothing, and put it in her coat, and said no more than that

known_facts.fact: She came to the cot after the night lamps without being asked, and said Wrong question before the Captain had asked one.
known_facts.evidence: "Wrong question," she said, before he had asked one.

known_facts.fact: She asked who signs the letter, and said that since the almoner does, it is his to say yes to, and he has.
known_facts.evidence: "Then it's his to say yes to, and he's said it."

known_facts.fact: She told the Captain to decide by the bell and not to sit up writing letters he has not decided to send, and that she wants both hands at the dawn forms.
known_facts.evidence: I'll want those hands at the dawn forms, both of them, so don't sit up writing letters you've not decided to send.

known_facts.fact: She does not do dogs, and re-splinted the hound anyway.
known_facts.evidence: "I don't do dogs."

known_facts.fact: She watched the Captain take his hand off the kennel grate, looked at the grate and at him, and left without a word.
known_facts.evidence: Maelis was watching the hand.

relationships.label: the knight whose knee she bound
relationships.note: She read his knee at the top of the Steps, bound it with emberthread when he chose her way off the mountain, and has said no fifteen times when he asked to go down; he does the dawn forms because she would know if he didn't, though he has no idea how.

relationships.label: keeper of the House's ledgers
relationships.note: Wren told Darrow that Maelis says her words in her sleep; Maelis says she doesn't sleep and Wren lies, and when Wren brought news of the list her eyes flicked to Maelis and away.

relationships.label: the other captain in her hall
relationships.note: He lies on the cot beside Darrow's and watched the weeks before the Binding from there; when Darrow asked what had begun, she looked down the hall at Hollis, then out at the snow, and told him to close the door instead of answering.

deeper: She was not surprised by the script of light, and she has not said why.
